name: Should I choose solid wood or MDF for kitchen trim and molding?

mainEntity.name: Should I choose solid wood or MDF for kitchen trim and molding?

acceptedAnswer.text: The choice comes down to appearance, budget, and long-term durability. Medium-density fiberboard (MDF) is cost-effective, perfectly flat, and takes paint smoothly without grain texture, making it common for painted crown and baseboards. However, MDF swells if exposed to standing water, which makes solid wood or moisture-resistant trim better suited around sink bases or dishwashers. Solid hardwoods like maple or oak offer superior impact resistance against vacuum bumps and dropped pans, and they allow for staining. If your kitchen trim will be painted, MDF or primed finger-jointed pine saves money, while high-moisture contact areas benefit from real wood.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use MDF for smooth painted ceilings and upper trim to save on costs, but choose solid wood around floors and wet zones for better moisture and impact resistance.
